content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the structures of graphene and fullerenes
Describe the structure and uses of buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀)
Explain the uses of carbon nanotubes

Graphene and fullerenes are relatively recently discovered forms of carbon with remarkable properties. They have revolutionised materials science and have potential applications in electronics, medicine, and engineering.
are different physical forms of the same element. Carbon has several allotropes:
is a single layer of graphite - a one-atom-thick sheet of carbon atoms arranged in hexagons.
One delocalised electron per carbon atom
The thinnest material known (one atom thick)
[DIAGRAM: Graphene structure showing hexagonal arrangement of carbon atoms]
Strong covalent bonds in all directions
are molecules of carbon atoms with hollow shapes - either spheres or tubes.
60 carbon atoms arranged in a sphere

Drug delivery (trap drugs inside, deliver to specific cells)
are cylindrical fullerenes - essentially rolled-up sheets of graphene.
Tube of hexagonally arranged carbon atoms
Graphene and fullerenes represent a new area of science called
- working with materials at the atomic and molecular scale.
Unique properties not found in bulk materials

Thinking graphene is a different element from graphite
Both are allotropes of carbon - same element, different structure
Thinking carbon nanotubes are solid rods
Carbon nanotubes are hollow tubes (like rolled graphene)
Confusing C₆₀ with a giant covalent structure
C₆₀ is a molecule (contains exactly 60 atoms)
Describe the structure of graphene. (3 marks)
Explain why graphene can conduct electricity. (2 marks)
State two properties of graphene that make it useful for making flexible electronic screens. (2 marks)
Describe the structure of buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀). (2 marks)
Carbon nanotubes are used to strengthen sports equipment such as tennis rackets. Explain why carbon nanotubes are suitable for this use. (3 marks)
Suggest why fullerenes can be used to deliver drugs to specific parts of the body. (3 marks)
